title: Sirt1 sustains Sonic hedgehog signaling to promote medulloblastoma progression through regulating Gli3 processing
task: Determine Sirt1 regulation of Sonic hedgehog signaling in medulloblastoma progression
key_results: Sirt1 is elevated in SHH-driven MB; Sirt1 deacetylates Gli3 to inhibit proteolytic processing into repressor form, sustaining SHH signaling; Sirt1 knockdown suppresses MB proliferation and extends survival; pharmacological Sirt1 inhibition shows therapeutic efficacy
comments: Well-designed study with clinical relevance; mechanistic insight into Sirt1-mediated deacetylation of Gli3 is clear, though off-target effects of Sirt1 inhibitors on other pathways warrant consideration.

model_io.model: primary mouse MB cells and orthotopic transplantation models

hypotheses.hypothesis: Sirt1 sustains SHH signaling by deacetylating Gli3 and blocking its conversion to repressor form
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; Sirt1 inhibition blocks pathway and impairs tumor progression

title: Decoding the CAF–TAM axis: multi-omics dissection and therapeutic targeting of stromal–immune crosstalk in the tumor microenvironment
task: Characterize CAF–TAM crosstalk and therapeutic targeting in tumor microenvironment
key_results: Multi-omics analysis identifies diverse CAF/TAM subpopulations with bidirectional signaling regulating immune suppression, metabolic adaptation, and angiogenesis
comments: This is a comprehensive review synthesizing recent multi-omics advances; lacks novel primary experimental data but provides valuable conceptual framework for TME reprogramming strategies.

model_io.model: tumor microenvironment tissues (single-cell, multi-omics, spatial profiling)

title: Aging-associated decline of phosphatidylcholine synthesis is a malleable trigger of natural mitochondrial aging
task: Identify mechanisms of natural mitochondrial aging and test dietary interventions
key_results: Phosphatidylcholine synthesis declines with age; dietary phosphatidylcholine supplementation restores mitochondrial integrity and metabolic resilience in C. elegans and human cells
comments: The finding that a single lipid class is both a natural aging trigger and reversible via diet is elegant, though the mechanistic link between PC levels and mitochondrial network disruption remains partially unexplored.

model_io.model: C. elegans (wild-type and long-lived mutants clk-1, isp-1)

hypotheses.hypothesis: Aging-associated PC decline drives mitochondrial dysfunction
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; PC supplementation restores function

title: Cluster assembly dynamics drive fidelity of planar cell polarity polarization

key_results: Cluster size correlates with polarization accuracy; larger clusters are more polarized; mutations blocking cluster growth impair tissue-level polarization

hypotheses.hypothesis: Larger PCP clusters achieve higher polarization fidelity through increased signal amplification

hypotheses.hypothesis: Transition to unequal cleavage causes divergence in BMP pathway function
